title: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind
author: William Kamkwamba & Bryan Mealer
description: The maize country of central Malawi, where the Kasungu plateau rolls east from the district town toward the trading centre of Wimbe. Through the 2001-02 famine a teenager on his family's farm teaches himself from library books and builds a windmill out of scrap, turning wind into light and water. The map runs from the farm and the little school at Wimbe out to the district town, and finally south to the capital.

route.summary: The story begins on a smallholding where the family grows maize and tobacco on the Kasungu plateau. When the rains fail and the 2001-02 famine takes hold, the teenage narrator has to leave school because his parents can no longer pay the fees. Hunger on this farm is what sets everything that follows in motion.
route.note: Kamkwamba's account places his family's maize farm at Masitala, a hamlet within the Wimbe area east of Kasungu town. Masitala is not a separately mapped point, so this pins the farm at the verified village of Wimbe.

route.summary: Out of school and short of food, the narrator keeps studying on his own at the modest community library by the local primary school. A worn textbook on energy, with a picture of a windmill on the cover, gives him the idea that would change his family's life. This little room of donated books is where the plan is born.
route.note: The book names the small library attached to the primary school at Wimbe, but no separate coordinate exists for the building; this marks a point within the verified village of Wimbe.

route.summary: The trading centre is the cluster of shops, market stalls and a scrapyard that serves the farming villages around Wimbe. The narrator combs it for a dynamo, tractor parts, bicycle bits and PVC pipe, hauling junk back to the farm to turn into a windmill. It is the hardware store of a place with almost no money.
route.note: Wimbe and its trading centre are named in the book; this marks the commercial heart of the village where the market and scrapyard sit.

route.summary: Kasungu is the district town about twenty kilometres west of Wimbe, the nearest place with a proper market, secondary schools and offices. It stands for the larger Malawi beyond the family farm, the town you reach for anything the village cannot supply, and a step on the narrator's path once word of his windmill spreads.
route.note: Kasungu is named in the book as the district town; this marks the town centre.

route.summary: Malawi's capital sits roughly two hours' drive south of Kasungu. Once bloggers and reporters pick up the story of the boy and his windmill, the capital becomes the gateway to the world beyond: flights, conferences and a return to formal schooling. It closes the arc that began with a hungry teenager reading in a village library.
route.note: Lilongwe is named in the book and lies about two hours south of Kasungu, well beyond the farming country the story is set in, so it is marked as an excursion outside the setting.
